"I guess," went a slightly softer voice while Mark leaned away, and "I'd have no reason not let them sell, would you either?"

"Look," Mark decided in his quietest voice possible after taking his final bite -–the last shred of uneaten sandwich hung heavy on his fork.

topic: A person finds their childhood home listed for sale online
story:
She took slow steps into that dimly lit old bedroom. The scent was there – same creaky door handle, old floorboard groans she and her friends used to make a deliberate contest out as children with wide open giggles when summer sunlight would spill from the morning room's doorway, though only this time a realtor stood near an unadorned wall with hands buried deep in pockets of his raincoat.

"Hello again..." the woman at his side whispered as if noticing something. Some sort of uneasy air had begun to cling inside her too after that glance fell on it -the faded watercolour above bedroom dresser now, almost indistinguishable from its white backdrop: an autumn sun tree with its topmost leaves all still held fast by some force other than gravity that must be real too, one that even held when she wasn't even a child anymore and yet stayed strong through the storm outside making tiny pattering on leafy branches below in this particular drawing...

Inside, something went slightly awry: for now those walls had finally stopped speaking.
